families.axis: a plea that concedes the fault it covers → a justification that clears the act outright

members.gloss: a defense of some offensive behavior or some failure to keep a promise etc.
members.tone: Admits the fault while covering it - what is being defended is already offensive behaviour or a promise broken, whereas *defence* presumes nothing against the act at all.

members.gloss: the justification for some act or belief
members.tone: The plain word for the justification of an act or belief, passing no verdict on whether it succeeds and presuming no wrongdoing the way *excuse* does.

members.gloss: the justification for some act or belief
members.tone: Carries the outcome inside it - the act or belief comes out justified, where *defence* only puts the case.

families.axis: a quick answer named neutrally → an answer marked as impudence

members.gloss: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
members.tone: Blunt reproof - the insolent answer reduced to sheer talk, named by the organ that produced it rather than by anything it said.

members.gloss: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
members.tone: Informal and curt where *mouth* is broad, it clips the impudent answer down to a single flick of cheek.

members.gloss: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
members.tone: Informal, and it hears spirit in the impudence that *lip* hears only offence in - still a rebuke, but an amused one.

members.gloss: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
members.tone: The plainest of these - it marks only that something came back quickly, leaving the wit or the criticism unremarked.

members.gloss: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
members.tone: Frames the quick reply as a move made against the first, so its wit or its criticism lands as opposition rather than mere answer.

members.gloss: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
members.tone: Formal and composed, dignifying the quick reply as a proper answer where *counter* casts it as a blow returned.

families.axis: hopes left unmet → trust broken and the person deserted

members.gloss: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
members.tone: Puts the weight on not being there when relied on, covering both the proving undependable and the walking away, but stated as a lapse rather than a wrong.

members.gloss: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
members.tone: The same desertion as *fail*, but framed as trust broken against the person left behind, which is why it is the heaviest word here.

members.gloss: fail to meet the hopes or expectations of
members.tone: The mildest of the three: hopes or expectations simply come up short, with none of *fail*'s claim that someone was depended on and abandoned.

families.axis: an offer dangled → the trap sprung

members.gloss: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
members.tone: The lightest of the three: a promise held out to someone still standing free of it, where *lure* already has them moving.

members.gloss: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
members.tone: Works by making the promise attractive rather than by baiting a spot, so the persuasion sounds pleasant even when it is the exaggerated kind.

members.gloss: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
members.tone: Draws the person somewhere rather than merely dangling something, and of the three it keeps the falseness of the promise nearest the surface.

members.gloss: lure by imitating the characteristic call of an animal
members.tone: Neutral and technical here: the enticement is a mimicked animal cry, so the whole of the deception sits in the sound and none of it in any promise.

members.gloss: entice and trap
members.tone: The enticing is only half of it — the closing of the trap is the other half, which is what makes this land harder than *entice*.

families.axis: not easily moved from a purpose → immovably fixed on it whatever the cost

members.gloss: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
members.tone: The evenest word here - determination as a level that never dips, without the hardness *firm* and *stiff* put into it.

members.gloss: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
members.tone: Resolution felt as something pressed against and not giving - resistance where *steady* offers only constancy.

members.gloss: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
members.tone: Unshakable, but by rigidity - the resolve reads as unbending as much as strong.

members.gloss: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
members.tone: The warmest of the unshakable four - firmness praised as something held faithfully over time.

members.gloss: characterized by great determination
members.tone: Says the will outright and says there is a lot of it, with none of the hardness metaphor carried by *firm* or *stiff*.

members.gloss: desperately determined
members.tone: Determination pushed to its extreme edge, where the resolve looks driven rather than chosen.

members.gloss: dependable
members.tone: Hearty approval - dependable in the way something sturdy is, solid enough to take weight.

members.gloss: fixed in your purpose
members.tone: States only that the purpose is fixed and passes no verdict on it, where *steadfast* and *stalwart* praise.

members.gloss: dependable
members.tone: Dependability raised to staunchness - stronger praise than *stout*, and it suggests standing by as well as standing up.

members.gloss: unshaken in purpose
members.tone: The purpose holds against something that might have cowed it - it implies the attempt was made and failed.

members.gloss: unshaken in purpose
members.tone: The flat negative of the same idea - the purpose simply did not move, without the note of fear faced down in *undaunted*.

members.gloss: firm in purpose or belief; characterized by firmness and determination
members.tone: Formal and settled, and it covers belief as well as purpose - firmness treated as a standing quality of the person, not a stand taken once.

members.gloss: beg persistently and urgently
members.tone: Pressing rather than abject - the force sits in refusing to let the asking drop, where *implore* puts it in the emotion behind it.

members.gloss: beg persistently and urgently
members.tone: Formal, and the persistence lands as a burden on the person asked, where *insist* marks only the asker's refusal to stop.

members.gloss: call upon in supplication; entreat
members.tone: The entreaty in its most formal dress, an appeal made in the posture of supplication rather than *beg*'s bare asking.

members.gloss: call upon in supplication; entreat
members.tone: Raises the same entreaty to a pitch of desperation that *beg* states flatly.

members.gloss: plead or ask for earnestly
members.tone: Asking in a formal key, urged by earnestness rather than by *importune*'s wearing repetition.

members.gloss: ask humbly (for something)
members.tone: The humility is the whole of it, stated outright and with ceremony, where *beg* leaves the asker's lowness implied.

families.axis: caution missing from practical dealings → a settled disposition to act headlong

members.gloss: a lack of caution in practical affairs
members.tone: Names the fault as an absence — caution simply not brought to practical affairs — and stops short of accusing anyone of charging ahead, which *rashness* does.

members.gloss: the trait of acting rashly and without prudence
members.tone: Heavier because it fixes the fault as a trait of the person rather than a gap in a decision: acting, and acting without prudence, not merely lacking it.

families.axis: a shortfall counted against a thing → a high quality counted admiringly in its favour

members.gloss: any admirable quality or attribute
members.tone: Presents an attribute as admirable in itself, already judged and approved, where *value* only weighs.

members.gloss: any admirable quality or attribute
members.tone: The same admirable attribute framed as something to a thing's credit, weighable point by point against *fault*.

members.gloss: the quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable
members.tone: Unsigned by design: it takes the quality positive or negative alike, so it appraises where *virtue* and *fault* have already decided.

members.gloss: the high value or worth of something
members.tone: Puts the height into the word itself - not worth but worth pitched high, where *worth* names the quality without ranking it.

members.gloss: the quality that renders something desirable or valuable or useful
members.tone: Plainly positive and broad, covering what makes a thing desirable, valuable or merely useful, with none of *price*'s insistence that the quality is great.
